title: Truth, and truthful living
hook: truth is higher than everything, and higher still is truthful living (Sri Rag, ang 62)
tomorrow: Deeds as soil, the Word as seed

segments.voice: Yesterday, ask about the light. Your line was see the light. Did you meet someone without the usual label? Today, one of the biggest words in the whole Granth, and a twist on it. Day two hundred forty-nine.
screen: `ASK ABOUT THE LIGHT — SEE THE LIGHT.`

segments.voice: Everybody knows someone who can win any argument about honesty. They can quote the rules, spot every white lie, explain exactly what truth is. And then you watch how they treat the waiter. Or the other way around: someone who never talks about truth at all, but whose word is solid, whose yes means yes, who returns the extra change. Which of them has more truth in them? Guru Nanak answered that question in one line, and it's one of the most quoted lines in Sikh life. Today's word is sach.
screen: `WINS EVERY ARGUMENT.` → `THEN, THE WAITER.` → `WHICH ONE HAS TRUTH?`

segments.voice: Sach means truth. And in the Guru Granth Sahib it's bigger than facts. Sach, or sat, is one of the names of God. Satnam, the True Name, comes right at the start of the Granth. And Japji Sahib opens by saying, in paraphrase: true in the beginning, true through the ages, true now, and, Nanak says, true forever. So truth isn't just something you tell. It's what's real, what lasts. Now the twist. On Ang 62, in Sri Rag, Guru Nanak sings: sachahu orai sabh ko upar sach aachaar. Everything is below truth; but higher still is truthful living. Aachaar means conduct, how you actually live. So there's something above even knowing the truth, and that's living it. The Gurus didn't separate belief and behavior. A person who speaks beautifully about God and cheats at work hasn't reached the top of the line. A farmer who never read a book, and whose dealings are straight, might have. This is why the Sikh way leans so hard on the everyday: kirat karni, earning honestly; vand chhakna, sharing; the plain promise that your word is good. Truth, for the Gurus, is something you can see in a person's hands and hear in their bargains. It's also why this is hard. Knowing truth takes a clever mind. Living it takes every small moment of the day, including the ones nobody sees.
screen: `SACH, SAT — A NAME OF GOD.` · `TRUE THEN, NOW AND FOREVER.` · `HIGHER STILL: TRUTHFUL LIVING.` · `SEEN IN HANDS AND BARGAINS.` · then, large: `TRUTH, LIVED.`

segments.voice: Think of one small truth you'd usually skip. Not a big confession, just a little one: I haven't read it yet. That was my mistake. I'm not fine, actually. I can't make it. Picture saying it, simply and kindly. Notice what fear comes up, and let it be there. Then decide whether you'll say it today. Rest with the breath, steady and plain. The bell holds the time.
Sach. Truth, and in the Granth a name of God, what's real and lasts. And higher still than truth, Guru Nanak says, is truthful living.
Your line: truth, lived. Today, tell the one small truth you'd usually skip, simply and kindly. Day two hundred forty-nine.

screen: `DAY 249 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: DEEDS AS SOIL, THE WORD AS SEED.`

howItsDone: Sikhs often quote Guru Nanak's line on truthful living (Ang 62) to describe the faith's emphasis on honest work, sharing and straight dealing in daily life, alongside remembering the Name.

match.prompt: inside Guru Nanak's line — tap the pairs.

myth: for Guru Nanak, knowing the truth is the highest thing
higher still, he says, is truthful living, sach aachaar.

Japji Sahib opens by calling God true in the beginning, now and forever

fork.setup: one person can explain truth perfectly but cheats at work. another never talks about it and deals straight. what does Guru Nanak's line put highest?
options: the one who explains truth best.
fork.reveal: sachahu orai sabh ko upar sach aachaar: everything is below truth, and higher still is truthful living.

original.note: Gurmukhi: sach, truth; in Gurbani it often carries a short final u sound in the spelling, sachu.

trapdoor: what you thought: truth means not telling lies.
what it means: in the Granth, truth is what's real and lasting, a name of God, and higher still is living it.
what a scholar hears: sach and sat both from the root for 'being'; Sri Rag Mahala 1, Ang 62, places aachaar, conduct, above truth itself.

sources.ref: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 62 (Sri Rag Mahala 1)
sources.quoted: sachahu orai sabh ko upar sach aachaar

sources.ref: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 1 (Japji Sahib, opening salok: aad sach jugaad sach)

notes: Ang 62 line quoted in transliteration (sachahu orai sabh ko upar sach aachaar); confirm the Ang and whether it belongs to an ashtapadi of Sri Rag Mahala 1.
The etymology of sach/sat from the Sanskrit root for 'being' (as-) is standard; confirm wording.
Kirat karni and vand chhakna were taught earlier in the path; this day refers to them without re-teaching.
